The small spread between temperature (-5°C) and dew point (-7°C) means the air is nearly saturated, but the clear skies suggest this is due to cold air mass rather than approaching precipitation. The strong NW winds at 40-60 km/h indicate a pressure gradient, likely from a passing high-pressure system. Wind chill will make it feel much colder. Excellent visibility confirms dry, clear conditions. Expect continued cold, dry weather with gradual warming as pressure stabilizes.

Fire weather danger is EXTREME: 35°C temperature, 15% humidity (critically low), strong gusty winds (50-80 km/h), and drought-dried vegetation create ideal conditions for rapid wildfire ignition and spread. Any fire that starts will be difficult to control. Dust storms are possible due to strong winds over dry, bare soil. The clear skies and high pressure (1018 hPa) indicate no rain relief. Heat stress is a risk for outdoor workers and livestock. Forecast: Continued hot, dry, and windy through the evening. Winds may decrease slightly after sunset but humidity will remain very low. Fire danger remains extreme for the next 24-48 hours with no precipitation expected.

items.answer: Morning forecast: The high dew point (21°C) and warm sea surface temperature (26°C) indicate abundant moisture. As the sun heats the land through the morning, convective activity will increase. The 40% stratocumulus will develop into cumulus and eventually cumulonimbus by early afternoon. The steady low pressure (1005 hPa) and southerly flow will maintain moisture supply from the sea. Expect: Morning - partly cloudy, warming to 28-30°C, humidity increasing. Afternoon - 60-70% chance of showers or thunderstorms as convection peaks. Evening - storms dissipate after sunset, clearing skies, temperature dropping to 23-24°C. Wind may shift and increase during storm activity.
